body.statement: The plug-in frontier \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\) is a \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable random element of \(C([0,1])\) and is computable from \(\{(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni}):1\le i\le n\}\), \(b\), and the declared finite-cell estimators, without \(\Delta_n\), \(u_n\), or \(E_n\). For every \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable \(\widehat t_n\) and every real \(x\), the deterministic inclusion \(\{\sup_{t\in[0,1]}T_n(t)\le x\}\subseteq\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le x\}\) holds. On \(0<\widehat t_n<1\), with \(\widehat c_n=\widehat t_n/(1-\widehat t_n)\), \(T_n(\widehat t_n)=(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n)\). Thus a uniform law or simultaneous coverage bound for the oracle path transfers exactly to a selector computed from the plug-in frontier; no approximation of the unobserved regret by \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\) is required.
body.justification: The lemma separates the observable frontier used to choose a temperature from the oracle regret path that the confidence envelope covers.
body.gap: Post-search arguments such as Kang's assume an observed indexed statistic, while the causal regret here contains an unobserved oracle comparator; the exact event inclusion supplies the needed operational bridge without a false plug-in equality.
body.consumer: A planner can compute a temperature from the displayed plug-in frontier and invoke the simultaneous oracle-regret certificate at precisely that observed-data choice.
